anonymous_voting_explained.intro: Anonymous voting means no one can link a ballot back to the person who cast it - while the result remains fully countable and verifiable. Here is how that is possible, and why it protects voters.

sections.heading: Why ballot secrecy matters
paragraphs: The secret ballot exists for a reason: when people fear their vote can be seen, they can be pressured, bribed or punished for it. Genuine anonymity is what lets people vote according to their conscience, especially in contested or sensitive decisions.

sections.heading: Anonymity vs pseudonymity
paragraphs: Many systems are only pseudonymous: votes are stored under an identifier that can, in principle, be linked back to a person. True anonymity means that link is broken in a way that cannot be reversed, even by the system's administrators.

sections.heading: How zero-knowledge cryptography helps
paragraphs: Zero-knowledge proofs let the system confirm something is true - for example, that a voter is eligible and has not already voted - without revealing the underlying identity. This is how a system can enforce one person, one vote and still keep the ballot anonymous.
The voter proves they have the right to vote; the system verifies that proof; and the ballot is recorded with no identity attached.

sections.heading: Anonymity without losing verifiability
paragraphs: The common fear is that secrecy makes a result impossible to check. With modern cryptography the opposite is true: ballots can be anonymous and the total can still be publicly verified. You get both privacy and proof.

takeaways: Ballot secrecy protects voters from coercion, bribery and retaliation.
Pseudonymity is not anonymity - the link to identity can be reversed.
Zero-knowledge proofs confirm eligibility without revealing identity.
Anonymous ballots can still be counted and verified.
Coercion resistance depends on genuine, irreversible anonymity.

blockchain_voting_myths_vs_reality.intro: Blockchain is one of the most hyped, and most misunderstood, words in digital voting. This guide separates what blockchain genuinely contributes to elections from what it does not.

sections.heading: Myth: blockchain alone makes voting secure
paragraphs: A blockchain is a tamper-evident, shared record. That is useful, but it does not by itself authenticate voters, keep ballots secret, or prove the count is correct. A vote stored on a blockchain can still be insecure if those properties are missing. Blockchain is a component, not a magic guarantee.

sections.heading: Reality: what blockchain does well
paragraphs: Where a public ledger helps is durability and transparency: once published, records are very hard to alter quietly, and anyone can read them. For voting, that supports auditability - observers can see the same data the organizers see, without relying on a private database.

sections.heading: Myth: blockchain means votes are public
paragraphs: A frequent worry is that putting votes 'on a blockchain' exposes them. It does not have to. Ballots are encrypted and anonymized before anything is published, so what is public is the verifiable record, not anyone's choice.

sections.heading: Reality: cryptography does the heavy lifting
paragraphs: The properties people actually want from a vote - secrecy, coercion resistance, verifiability - come from cryptography such as zero-knowledge proofs, not from the ledger itself. The right way to think about it: cryptography provides the guarantees, and a ledger can make the resulting evidence public and durable.

takeaways: Blockchain is a tamper-evident record, not a complete voting system.
It does not by itself provide authentication, secrecy or a provable count.
Votes can be on a public ledger and still be secret and anonymous.
Cryptography, not the ledger, provides the core voting guarantees.
Judge a system by its guarantees and evidence, not by buzzwords.
blockchain_voting_myths_vs_reality.title: Blockchain voting: myths vs reality

how_secure_online_voting_works.intro: Secure online voting is not a single feature - it is a chain of guarantees, from confirming who can vote to proving the final count is correct. This guide explains that chain in plain language.

sections.heading: What 'secure' really means for a vote
paragraphs: A poll and a binding election look similar on screen, but they are not the same thing. A binding vote has to satisfy several properties at once: only eligible people can vote, each votes once, ballots stay secret, and the published result provably matches what voters chose. Security is the combination of all of these, not any single one.
When a vendor says a system is 'secure', the useful question is always: secure against what, and how can we check? Good systems answer with evidence, not adjectives.

sections.heading: Step 1: authentication and the census
paragraphs: Every vote starts with a census - the list of who is eligible. Voters authenticate against that list so the system can confirm eligibility and enforce one person, one vote, without that identity later being attached to their ballot.
The strength of authentication should match the stakes. A small club vote might use an email link, while a high-stakes election may require stronger identity checks.

sections.heading: Step 2: casting a secret ballot
paragraphs: When a voter makes a choice, a secure system encrypts the ballot on their device before it ever leaves. Cryptographic techniques then separate the voter's identity from the encrypted ballot, so that no one - not administrators, not the platform - can link a person to how they voted.

sections.heading: Step 3: counting with proof
paragraphs: At the close of voting, ballots are tallied and the result is published together with cryptographic proof. In an end-to-end verifiable system, each voter can confirm their own ballot was included, and anyone can verify that the published total is the correct sum of all valid ballots.
This is the difference between 'trust us' and 'check for yourself'. The result does not depend on trusting the vendor, because the math is open to inspection.

sections.heading: Why open source matters
paragraphs: If the code that runs an election is secret, its security rests on the vendor's word. Open-source voting infrastructure lets independent experts inspect exactly how votes are handled, which is why public scrutiny, not obscurity, is the stronger foundation for trust.

takeaways: Security in voting is a chain: eligibility, single voting, secrecy and a provable count.
Authentication confirms who can vote without linking identity to the ballot.
Ballots are encrypted on the voter's device and unlinked from identity.
End-to-end verifiability lets anyone check the result without trusting the platform.
Open-source code makes security inspectable rather than assumed.

how_to_prevent_election_fraud_online.intro: Fear of fraud is the main reason organizations hesitate to vote online. The good news: the same risks exist on paper, and a well-designed digital system addresses them more transparently. Here is how.

sections.heading: Know the real risks
paragraphs: Election fraud is not one thing. The main risks are: ineligible people voting, people voting more than once, ballots being altered or lost, the count being manipulated, and voters being coerced. A serious system has a specific defense for each, rather than a vague promise of being 'secure'.

sections.heading: Authentication and one person, one vote
paragraphs: Strong authentication against the census prevents ineligible voting, and the system enforces a single ballot per voter. Matching the strength of authentication to the stakes is part of good design.

sections.heading: Tamper-evidence and a verifiable count
paragraphs: Encrypted ballots and a tamper-evident record make it obvious if anything is altered. An end-to-end verifiable tally means manipulation of the count is not just prohibited - it is detectable by anyone, because the published proof would not check out.

sections.heading: Coercion resistance and open scrutiny
paragraphs: Genuine ballot secrecy removes the ability to buy or coerce votes, because no one can prove how they voted. And open-source code lets security researchers find and fix weaknesses in the open, which is far safer than hoping a closed system has no flaws.

takeaways: Fraud is several distinct risks, each needing a specific defense.
Authentication and single-ballot enforcement stop ineligible and double voting.
Encryption and tamper-evidence reveal any attempt to alter ballots.
A verifiable count makes manipulation detectable by anyone.
Secrecy resists coercion, and open source exposes flaws to be fixed.

Give proper notice and let the platform confirm quorum automatically.

Documentation is what makes a digital AGM defensible.

verifiable_voting_explained.intro: Verifiable voting means you do not have to trust the people running the election - you can check the result yourself. This guide explains end-to-end verifiability and why it is becoming the standard for serious digital votes.

sections.heading: The problem with 'trust us'
paragraphs: In most digital systems, you trust the operator to report results honestly. For a vote, that is a weak foundation: the operator could make a mistake, be compromised, or be accused of bias even when honest. Verifiability replaces trust with proof.

sections.heading: What end-to-end verifiability means
paragraphs: End-to-end verifiability (often shortened to E2E-V) gives two guarantees. 'Recorded as cast' means each voter can confirm their ballot was captured correctly. 'Counted as recorded' means anyone can verify that the final tally is the correct sum of all recorded ballots.
Crucially, these checks reveal nothing about how any individual voted. Verifiability and secrecy are not in tension - a well-designed system delivers both.

sections.heading: How voters and observers check a result
paragraphs: Each voter receives a way to confirm their ballot is included in the final set, typically through a tracker that does not reveal their choice. Independent observers can download the encrypted ballots and the proofs and re-run the verification themselves.
Because the data and the method are public, no single party, including the vendor, has to be trusted for the result to be believed.

sections.heading: Why it matters for legitimacy
paragraphs: A result that can be independently verified is far harder to dispute. When a vote is close or politically charged, verifiability is what turns 'we counted and you have to believe us' into 'here is the proof, check it'.
International guidance on e-voting, such as the Council of Europe's recommendations, points organizations toward exactly this kind of transparency and evidence.

takeaways: Verifiable voting replaces trust in the operator with checkable proof.
End-to-end verifiability covers both that your vote was recorded and that the count is correct.
Verification reveals nothing about how anyone voted.
Independent observers can re-run the checks themselves.
Verifiability is what makes a contested result defensible.

1.content: Nous avons choisi Vocdoni car la solution garantit une participation sûre, fiable et transparente à tous nos membres lors de l'assemblée générale annuelle.
1.handle: Directeur général · Centre Excursionista de Catalunya
1.title: Une participation sûre et transparente

2.content: Le choix de Vocdoni a été clair. À Òmnium Cultural, nous avons misé sur un système de vote sûr et vérifiable nous permettant de tenir nos assemblées statutaires avec toutes les garanties.
2.title: Toutes les garanties pour 180 000 membres

3.content: Vocdoni nous offre un système de vote facile, sûr, anonyme et évolutif, parfaitement intégré à notre environnement institutionnel. Nous continuerons à lui faire confiance, sans hésiter !
3.handle: Directeur informatique · Ordre des ingénieurs industriels de Catalogne
3.platform_name: Ordre des ingénieurs industriels de Catalogne
3.title: Un vote facile, sûr et évolutif

4.content: Vocdoni nous permet d'organiser des votes avec des membres de tous les territoires de langue catalane à égalité de conditions. Le décompte instantané simplifie nos assemblées et garantit une transparence totale. Nous apprécions tout particulièrement le fait qu'il soit entièrement disponible en catalan.
4.title: Vote dans tous les territoires de langue catalane

5.content: Offrir aux membres un système de vote sûr et fiable est essentiel, surtout en période de pandémie. Vocdoni nous a fourni un outil facile à utiliser qui a simplifié le processus de vote et stimulé la participation.
5.title: Un vote sûr qui a stimulé la participation

6.content: Préparer l'ensemble du processus de vote et centraliser tous les outils pour l'assemblée a été facile, intuitif et clair. Les membres ont salué l'organisation et la simplicité d'utilisation. Même dans un secteur peu technologique, nous avons obtenu une forte participation - les gens ont particulièrement apprécié de pouvoir voter à l'avance sans se déplacer. Lorsque nous avons rencontré un petit souci avec la liste, le support technique a été rapide et professionnel.
6.handle: Responsable informatique · Associació de Guies Habilitats de Catalunya
6.title: Facile à mettre en place et forte participation malgré un public peu technophile

7.content: Vocdoni a porté notre vote Bisbalenc/a de l'Any, augmentant la participation citoyenne et apportant transparence, sécurité et résultats instantanés sur la blockchain. Nous avons apprécié sa sécurité, son évolutivité, sa vérifiabilité universelle et sa flexibilité. En 2023, le vote hybride a aussi été rendu possible, simplifiant grandement l'ensemble du processus.
7.handle: Chargé de la participation citoyenne · Mairie de La Bisbal d'Empordà
7.title: Un vote numérique transparent, sûr et flexible pour la citoyenneté

8.content: La transition vers le vote électronique devient inévitable, alors que la société est plus prête au numérique que jamais. Grâce au partenariat entre BLOOCK et Vocdoni, nous rendons possible une participation citoyenne plus significative et continue dans le gouvernement et les institutions.
8.title: Rendre possible une participation citoyenne significative

9.content: La numérisation de nos votes avec Vocdoni a amélioré l'efficacité de l'ensemble du processus électoral. Nous avons grandement facilité la participation, en particulier pour les membres qui ne pouvaient pas se déplacer, tout en maintenant un système agile et fiable.
9.handle: Président · Ordre officiel des infirmiers de Séville
9.title: Des votes plus efficaces et accessibles

10.content: À l'Ordre officiel des infirmiers de Barcelone, nous faisons confiance à Vocdoni pour l'ensemble de nos processus participatifs, en garantissant que les membres puissent exercer leur droit depuis n'importe où. Nous apprécions tout particulièrement l'instantanéité du décompte, la simplicité du système et la réactivité ainsi que l'accompagnement efficaces du support technique, qui rendent l'ensemble du processus agile, transparent et fiable.
10.handle: Responsable de projets · Ordre officiel des infirmiers de Barcelone
10.title: Une participation rapide, simple et fiable

11.content: En tant qu'Associazione Termotecnica Italiana, section Friuli Venezia Giulia, nous avons choisi de numériser notre gouvernance afin de faciliter la participation des professionnels. Vocdoni s'est imposée comme la solution idéale, se distinguant par sa simplicité, ses coûts et ses garanties.
11.title: Une gouvernance numérique qui facilite la participation

12.content:
À Esquerra Republicana, nous avons un engagement ferme envers la démocratie interne et la participation des membres. C'est pourquoi nous considérons qu'il est indispensable de disposer d'outils qui garantissent la plus grande intégrité, transparence et confidentialité dans tous les processus de vote.

Nous faisons confiance à Vocdoni depuis des années car il nous offre un système sécurisé, vérifiable et facile à utiliser, qui nous permet d'organiser des votes numériques avec toutes les garanties et adaptés aux besoins de notre organisation.
12.handle: Secrétaire nationale de l'Adhésion, de la Lutte Antirépressive et du Bien-être Émotionnel · Esquerra Republicana
12.title: Démocratie interne avec toutes les garanties

13.content: Chez «Granollers Primàries», nous comprenons la participation numérique comme un outil clé pour élargir et faciliter la participation citoyenne. C'est pourquoi nous cherchions une plateforme garantissant neutralité, transparence et sécurité maximale dans les processus de vote. Vocdoni offre tout cela et c'est pour cette raison que nous l'avons choisi pour nos primaires et prévoyons de continuer à l'utiliser dans de futures consultations.
13.handle: Responsable de la communication · Granollers Primàries
13.title: Participation numérique pour des primaires transparentes
